mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and real retail sales (implied by RSAFS growth) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their 12-month MA for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate coinciding with a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over four consecutive months signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) persistently above their 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months indicate a robust residential construction cycle, which supports demand for building materials and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month MA for eight consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).
